messages:
Alex Chen: heads-up — customer AcmePayments reports they removed a handful of users from their Okta group but those users still have the admin role in our app after the SCIM sync. They say the removals happened ~2025-12-20T08:45Z but access persists.

Lee Morales: do we have the Okta audit/export? can they paste the events so we can correlate?

Alex Chen: pasted below from their Okta logs and what we see in our scim-audit. Okta shows a group rename then a membership PATCH that removes members. Our endpoint returned 200 for the PATCH but downstream role assignment didn't update.

OktaBot: Okta event: 2025-12-20T08:41:10Z GROUP_RENAME id=00g9x8y7z externalId=acme-admins-v3 previousExternalId=acme-admins
OktaBot: Okta event: 2025-12-20T08:44:57Z GROUP_PATCH id=00g9x8y7z members=[u-321,u-654] performed_by=system-provisioner

Alex Chen: their SCIM PATCH payload (copied):

```json
{
  "Operations": [
    { "op": "remove", "path": "members[value eq \"u-321\"]" },
    { "op": "remove", "path": "members[value eq \"u-654\"]" }
  ]
}
```

Alex Chen: our scim-audit showed:

```
2025-12-20T08:44:57Z [INFO] PATCH /Groups?id=00g9x8y7z externalId=acme-admins-v3 status=200 time=95ms
2025-12-20T08:44:57Z [DEBUG] lookup_group_by_external_id(acme-admins-v3) -> NONE
2025-12-20T08:44:57Z [DEBUG] created local_group id=g-222 name="acme-admins-v3" mapped_role=NONE
```

Alex Chen: looks like we created a new local group record for the renamed externalId and didn't migrate the mapping from the old record (acme-admins -> role-admin). So the removals hit the new empty-mapping group and the old group record still holds the role grants.

Maria Gupta: this reads like a classic rename + membership race. Okta sometimes emits rename then membership updates referencing either id or new externalId depending on timing. If our create-on-miss path only checks externalId we get duplicates.

Jordan Park: added eng. quick theory: create-if-missing path does only externalId lookup and never checks source_id (Okta's group id) or the previousExternalId field. We should prefer a lookup by source_id when present, and if we create, migrate mapping from any existing record with matching source_id or previousExternalId. Proposed minimal fix: on group create-on-miss, if payload includes an "id" or previousExternalId, run a secondary lookup by source_id OR by previousExternalId, and if found, copy mapping and mark as renamed instead of creating duplicate.

Jordan Park: repro I ran locally:
1) seed DB: group external_id="acme-admins" -> mapped role role-admin
2) simulate Okta rename event (PUT/POST for acme-admins-v3 with source_id=00g9x8y7z)
3) simulate PATCH removing members against external_id acme-admins-v3
Observed: new group g-222 created, old mapping left behind on old record.

Lee Morales: temporary workaround for customers is manual: in Console search for group records by source_id (Okta id) and reassign the role mapping to the new group record, then re-run membership sync or remove users. Not great at scale.

SRE Oncall: @jordan_park please ensure any DB migration is transactional and feature-flagged. We should add a dry-run mode that logs intended migrations without changing data so we can scan tenants for duplicates first.

Jordan Park: agree. Plan:
- hotfix: update create-if-missing path to check payload.id (source_id) and previousExternalId; if a match is found, migrate mapping instead of creating duplicate. Ship to canary with feature flag=on/off and dry-run default=true.
- infra: add daily reconcile job to detect multiple local groups sharing the same source_id and produce alerts.
- telemetry: metric for duplicate_groups_by_source_id and an alert if >0 for any org.

Alex Chen: customer worried this was caused by token scope. They used a SCIM token with scopes ["scim:groups.write"]. I double-checked — we returned 200s and auth checks passed; not a scope issue.

Maria Gupta: added: confirm in the fix we don't change auth behavior. The bug is mapping logic.

Jordan Park: opening PR with unit/integration tests covering both orderings: rename->patch and patch->rename. Also including a migration utility and a non-destructive dry-run flag. Will request SRE review.

OpsBot: CI started for branch fix/scim-group-mapping-lookup (build 4590) :building_construction:

Lee Morales: support note drafted and sent: summarized root cause (rename + create-on-miss -> duplicate group), manual remediation steps, and our ETA for a pilot fix. Customer replied they can wait for a global fix but want notification when rolled to their org.

Jordan Park: QA notes for reviewer:
- simulate both event orderings and confirm no orphan mappings
- ensure when dry-run=true we log what we'd change but don't modify DB
- test rollback and idempotency of the migration path

SRE Oncall: request: add transaction-safe unique index test to ensure we don't create a race that produces two records simultaneously. Also ensure feature flag gating.

Alex Chen: I'll keep the customer updated. Lee please paste the manual remediation steps into the ticket (search by source_id -> reassign mapping -> remove stale group record) and mark as done when they confirm.

OpsBot: deploy pipeline started for build 4590 :rocket:

Jordan Park: canary looks fine at 10% after 1 hour. Flipping dry-run=false for AcmePayments org only. Monitoring duplicate_groups_by_source_id metric.

Lee Morales: customer confirmed manual changes removed access for the 5 affected users. They asked for a postmortem once the fix is fully in prod.

Jordan Park: rolling to 100% with feature flag on and migration enabled after additional checks pass.

Maria Gupta: once prod is stable let's add a quick runbook for Support: how to check for duplicate groups, how to reassign mapping, and how to request a retroactive merge for other customers.

-- end of thread --
